title: Ledger-backed offline usage collector and deterministic reconcile for Private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Private/VPC customers operating air-gapped or heavily firewalled deployments need a robust, auditable mechanism to export usage and quota events for upstream billing and quota enforcement. Current ad-hoc CSV exports are fragile: they lack monotonic checkpoints, are not idempotent, and lead to duplicated tokens or missed deductions when imports are delayed or retried. This causes incorrect billing, quota drift, and customer-facing rate-limit surprises.

Goal: Design and implement a ledger-backed offline usage collector and import/reconciliation flow that guarantees: monotonic sequence and cryptographic integrity of export bundles; idempotent server-side apply; deterministic conflict resolution on delayed imports; clear operational visibility (applied, pending, rejected); and safe retroactive billing adjustments when late data arrives. The system should work for both single-tenant Private installs and our Dedicated pools when customers request air-gapped export.

Non-goals: We are not implementing a full streaming replication protocol or real-time enforcement inside the air-gapped network. This ticket focuses on export bundle format, signing/checkpoint semantics, server import apis, reconciliation policy, and UX ramifications (console + runbook).

Success metrics:
- Zero duplicated token-count incidents reported in billing ops for Private deployments after rollout.
- End-to-end import idempotency tested with 3x retry scenarios.
- Time to reconcile a 48-hour delayed bundle <= 6 minutes (server apply time) for 100k events.
- Ability to map late events to invoices/credit adjustments with audit trail present in console.

Design proposal (summary):
1) Export bundle format: tar.gz archive containing a newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) file of usage events and a top-level manifest.json. Manifest fields: exporter_id, monotonic_checkpoint (64-bit integer), start_ts, end_ts, event_count, events_sha256, manifest_sha256, signer_key_id, signature. Events must include: event_id (UUIDv7), sequence_index (monotonic within exporter), type (generation|embedding|token_cache_hit), tokens, model, route, local_timestamp, rate_limit_bucket_id (optional), tenant_id (when present).

2) Ledger semantics: Each exporter instance (collector service in-customer) maintains a local monotonic checkpoint. The manifest.checkpoint is strictly increasing per exporter_id. Server will reject manifests with checkpoint <= last_applied_checkpoint for that exporter_id (idempotency). Server will accept checkpoints > last_applied_checkpoint and atomically apply contained events. Partial apply is NOT allowed: we validate events_sha256 and manifest signature before apply.

3) Signing and integrity: Use ECDSA-P256 with keys provisioned via customer KMS or ephemeral local key, with signer_key_id included in manifest. For air-gapped customers that cannot use cloud KMS, allow customer-provided public key registration over an out-of-band channel. Signature verifies manifest and events blob hash.

4) Server API for import: POST /v1/private/usage/import with multipart upload or presigned S3 location. Server responds with 202 Accepted and a job_id. Import states: pending_validation -> validated -> applying -> applied | rejected. Validation errors must be deterministic and surfaced with clear diagnostics (bad signature, checksum mismatch, missing fields, non-monotonic sequence).

5) Reconciliation policy for delayed imports: If events arrive after downstream billing window closed, we will: ingest as historical data; mark associated invoices as "provisional_adjustment" and create a ledger delta record. UX will require explicit invoice adjustment workflow (auto-credit optionally enabled via customer-level policy). Imports that change quota consumption retroactively do NOT retroactively throttle upstream requests; they only affect billing and future quota windows.

6) Rate-limit token-bucket reconciliation: Exported events include rate_limit_bucket_id and tokens_consumed. For persistent buckets we apply a deterministic algorithm: server replays events in sequence order per bucket to recompute final bucket state for reporting. If a late event causes a bucket to go negative historically, we do NOT revoke already-granted responses; we surface this as a usage anomaly and bill/credit accordingly.

7) Idempotency keys and dedupe: The server computes a manifest global_id = sha256(exporter_id + manifest.checkpoint + manifest_sha256). This becomes the idempotency key. Duplicate uploads with same global_id are ignored with 200 OK and a pointer to previous job.

8) Operational tooling: Console will expose import history, manifest details, and a per-exporter checkpoint timeline. Alerting rules for: repeated rejected manifests, large historical deltas (>10% of billed tokens/day), and long pending_validation times (>10 minutes). Provide a runbook for ops with commands to backfill, force-apply (for emergencies), and roll back adjustments.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full canonical ledger vs per-exporter monotonic checkpoints: per-exporter checkpoints keep exporter complexity low and support offline writes; cross-exporter ordering would require global consensus which is infeasible offline.
- Strict atomic apply delays visibility until verified; alternative is streaming apply with tombstones, but that complicates idempotency and increases risk of partial duplicates.
- Signing adds operational overhead for customers without KMS; we mitigate with simple key registration flow and clear docs.

Open questions:
- Should we allow imports that intentionally overlap previous checkpoint ranges (for replays) with a special "replay" flag and manual review?
- What authorization model for presigned upload endpoints for air-gapped customers who cannot perform outgoing calls?

Deliverables:
- Exporter format spec (Confluence doc + JSON schema)
- Server import endpoint and job lifecycle implementation
- Console UI for import audit and invoice adjustments
- Runbook and e2e test harness (simulated delayed uploads, retries, corrupted manifests)
comments: 2025-11-13 - Aisha Patel: Spiked on local exporter proof-of-concept. Verified we can produce NDJSON + manifest and sign with local ECDSA key. Initial tests show manifest verification and checksuming are fast for 100k events (~2s).

2025-11-18 - Marco Liu: Architecture review notes: prefer sha256 global_id over UUID to make idempotency deterministic across uploader implementations. Also proposing job-based server ingest so we can do async validation without blocking the uploader.

2025-11-20 - Priya Shah (Security): Requested key rotation plan and KMS dead-man switch; flagged legal requirement to retain audit chain for 7 years for some regulated customers. Marked security_review_required=true.

2025-11-26 - Marco Liu: Implemented initial server validator prototype on feature/ledger-import. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/server/pull/4021. Needs schema tests and signed-manifest verification added. Also added unit test for duplicate manifest upload dedupe.

2025-11-30 - Billing Ops (notes): For retroactive adjustments, prefer creating adjustment journal entries rather than rewriting invoices. Need mapping guidelines for Tax reporting team. Opening PM follow-up: PM-2741.

2025-12-02 - UX (Natalie Greenspan): Draft console panel showing 'Import history' and 'Pending adjustments' uploaded to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/private-usage-imports. Asking for fields to surface: exporter_id, checkpoint, event_count, errors, adjustment_amount.
